Independent re-review complete. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE the component-preserving repair on static/trace grounds, conditioned on an actual dynamic run of tests/test-branding.sh (outside this reviewer) confirming GREEN before delivery — dynamic execution is blocked by CLI approval in this sandbox (confirmed: `bash tests/test-branding.sh` and `python3 -m pytest --version` both returned "This command requires approval"), so no PASS/FAIL evidence from a live run in THIS session is claimed. This matches SPEC.md acceptance criterion 8 ("Sandbox-required test execution remains an environmental permission request, not a stage waiver") and the task instruction to state tests not executed rather than fabricate results.

Defect-class verification: the disclosed bug (a raw symlink target containing a symlink-component directory followed by '..', where naive lexical normalization collapses to the expected source but real OS resolution follows the symlink component first and lands outside the project) is traced end-to-end against the current uncommitted scripts/nightshift-branding.py. safe_source() (line 55) walks the target path one component at a time via lstat, and when it encounters the pivot symlink component it reads its real target and immediately rejects with AuditError('external') if that target is outside the project root (line 92-93) — before any stat/read of the disguised final file. mapped_link_source() (line 104) uses lexical(target) only as a cheap pre-filter (line 121) and always re-validates via safe_source(target, project) (line 124) as the authoritative, component-preserving check; a mismatch between the lexically-collapsed alias and the actually-resolved path raises 'external' (line 131) even when the pre-filter alone would have passed. This is called uniformly from both the leaf case (installed_path, line 333-351, used for root-level symlinked files and symlinked tree roots) and the tree-descendant case (installed_tree, line 353-394, used for nested symlinks inside a copied tree) — both code paths share one implementation, so the fix applies to both, though only the leaf/root case has a dedicated adversarial test.

Chronology corroborates a genuine RED→GREEN repair, not a rewritten narrative: tests/test-branding.sh mtime 13:58:37 (test added before sealing) → bot-sealed at commit 6343bc4 (14:00:41, diff confirmed via `git show`, adds exactly test_installed_dotdot_link_cannot_disguise_external_target, no other assertions touched) → docs/19/receipts/dotdot-nightshift-19-dotdot-test-red.log (14:01:54) shows exactly that one test FAILED ("0 != 1") against the pre-fix scanner with the other 15 tests passing → docs/19/receipts/code-review-resolution.md (14:01) records the static reviewer's miss and blocks the gate → scripts/nightshift-branding.py mtime 14:02:52, i.e. edited only after RED was captured. No receipt in docs/19/receipts/ postdates 14:02:52, so there is no artifact demonstrating a live GREEN run of the sealed regression against the current repaired scanner from any prior session either — this must still happen outside this reviewer before delivery.

No remaining contradiction with the earlier static review: docs/19/code-review.out.json's 17 claims (ownership boundary, exact-symlink-proves-ownership, unknown-copy-unread, output privacy, finite provider rules, policy self-consistency, coverage caps, install order, early --check placement) concern properties orthogonal to component-vs-lexical symlink target resolution — none of its claims characterize how '..' after a symlink component is resolved, so its APPROVE-conditional-on-dynamic-checks verdict is not falsified by the newly found defect; code-review-resolution.md explicitly states "The static reviewer did not identify this defect," which matches what is observable in that file (dotdot/pivot/component resolution is absent from its claims list). Both documents are consistent: prior review approved a narrower property set; the parent/independent-tester review found an orthogonal gap in a property the static review never actually traced.

One coverage gap noted (not a defect): mapped_link_source's relative-symlink branch (lines 112-120, entered only when os.readlink() returns a non-absolute path) is exercised by no test in tests/test-branding.sh — every constructed symlink in the suite uses an absolute target. Manual trace shows it is sound (leading '..' components are popped via Path.parent, which is safe only because installed_path/installed_tree already guarantee no ancestor of the symlink's own position is itself a symlink; the resulting target is still re-validated by the same safe_source() component walk before use), but this is asserted by code reading, not by a fixture, and no relative-symlink production path currently exists in install.sh's own copy/symlink modes (which always emit absolute targets), so the residual risk is low. Recommend flagging for a follow-up fixture rather than blocking this delivery.

Out of scope for this fix and unchanged from the prior review's own disclosure: untracked scripts/__pycache__/ and .nightshift.toml remain present in the worktree; the prior reviewer attributed these to a concurrent process in this shared managed worktree, and nothing in this pass implicates the branding/dotdot repair in producing them.
